text:
River Duero, river Duero,
no one comes down to keep you company;
no one stops to hear
your eternal stanza of water.


Indifferent or afraid,
the city turns its back.
It will not see in your mirror
its toothless wall.


You, old Duero, smile
among your silver beards,
grinding with your ballads
the poor harvests.


And among stone saints
and magical poplars
you pass, carrying in your waves
words of love, words.


Who could, like you,
both still and moving,
always sing the same verse
but with different water?


River Duero, river Duero,
no one comes down to be with you,
no one wants to heed
your eternal, forgotten stanza,


but lovers,
who ask about their souls
and sow in your foam
words of love, words.

translation.title: Ballad of the Duero
